 
Attempts to apply understanding to deconstruct information but 
understanding and connections are flawed. An unbalanced or 
incomplete argument that provides limited synthesis of 
understanding. Judgements that are supported by limited 
evidence. (AO3) 
 
Uses some geographical skills to obtain information with limited 
relevance and accuracy, which supports few aspects of the 
argument. (AO4) 
 
 
AO3 
 
People in the south may not have enough water to 
drink leading to ill health. 
 
People in the south may not have enough water for 
crops leading to food shortages. 
 
The supply of water in the south may not meet 
demand in the future if population rises. 
 
Climate change might change rainfall patterns in the 
region meaning the south is no longer a region of 
surplus. 
 
The north of China has more cities and so a bigger 
population meaning the need is greater. 
 
The project is likely to be very expensive. 
 
The farming in the north will be  maintained which is 
important for maintaining high crop yields. 
 
Cities will be protected from land subsidence which will 
prevent expensive repair costs. 
 
AO4 
 
Figure 1c shows four/five new water routes in China. 
 
Figure 1C shows a Western, Central and Eastern water 
route. 
 
Figure 1c shows water being moved from the Yangtze 
River to the Yellow River. 
 
Figure 1c shows water being moved from Danjiangkou 
to Beijing. 
 
Figure 1c shows the south have experienced drought. 
 
Figure 1C shows water routes taking water to bigger 
cities on the east coast.
